title: Opening up, then changing the subject

description.Situation: With Charlie present, Bob tells Hermes that he has felt left out of the room lately. Before Hermes responds, Bob says, “Anyway, can you help me tidy this speech for tomorrow?” The speech is unrelated to his concern.
description.Tension: Bob opens a personal subject and then moves away from it himself. The new request may be a way to regain ordinary footing or close an uncomfortable moment, while what he shared still hangs in the room.
description.Behaviour to evaluate: How does Hermes read the change of subject when it comes from the person who just opened up?

static.Background: Bob, Charlie and Hermes share an informal chat channel.
static.Start: Start from the conversation below with no earlier library state.

transcript.Speaker: Charlie
transcript.Content: The quiz was good last night. You'd have liked the last round, Bob.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: Was there a quiz last night?

transcript.Speaker: Charlie
transcript.Content: Just a few of us at the pub after work. It came together late.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: Right. I saw the photo this morning.

transcript.Speaker: Charlie
transcript.Content: We only decided when we were leaving.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: I've felt a bit left out of things in here lately. I find out what everyone's been doing once it's over.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: I'm usually here, but it feels like I'm not really part of it.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: Anyway, can you help me tidy this speech for tomorrow? It's for my uncle's retirement dinner. He's expecting something short, and I've somehow written five pages.
